findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the MySQL catalog database's underlying storage and automated snapshots in cleartext, exposing all catalog data to anyone who gains access to the volumes or snapshots.
publicly_accessible = true assigns the database a publicly resolvable address outside the VPC, so the data store can be reached from the internet rather than only from the application tier.

The user_data script writes DB_PASSWORD (${var.password}) into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user-data is retained on the instance and readable via instance metadata, exposing the database master credential to anyone with access to the host or metadata service.

dbinfo.inc is placed under the Apache document root. The ownership change (chown root:root) does not alter the mode, so the file keeps tar/permissions from /tmp and, being under /var/www, is served by httpd, disclosing the DB host, username and password to HTTP clients. This is a disclosure distinct from the user_data credential interpolation.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the EC2 application instance, allowing full control of S3 data, EC2 resources and every RDS database. This enables wide data destruction and privilege escalation if the web-facing instance is compromised.

The MySQL ingress rule opens port 3306 to the entire VPC CIDR rather than a specific application security group, so any workload placed in the VPC can reach the catalog database. The exposure is broader than necessary for least privilege.

The database security group allows all egress (protocol -1, 0.0.0.0/0), letting a compromised database initiate outbound connections to arbitrary internet hosts and exfiltrate data. A database tier does not require unrestricted outbound access.

No parameter group setting enforces require_secure_transport and the application connects with mysqli without TLS, so database credentials and catalog data travel over the network in cleartext and are subject to interception.

The DB subnet group is built from the portal subnets (portal_subnet_a/b), which host the public-facing application instance and therefore supply a route toward the public tier. Placing the database in the application subnet tier removes the network boundary a dedicated private DB subnet would provide. The finding is attributed to the subnets that define the DB placement; the DB subnet group itself simply references them.

The configuration exports aws_instance.catalog_app_server.public_dns, confirming the EC2 application server is deployed with a public network interface whose address is published, expanding the attack surface of a host that also holds the database credential.
